transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-09
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Sana Patel (Redwood SE), Theo Ramirez (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Medivance Head of Platform), Maya Chen (Medivance Security Lead), Ravi Singh (Medivance CTO), Olivia Park (Medivance DevOps)

Summary:
Quick scoping call to align on Private networking (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), region/data residency constraints, egress requirements, and concrete success criteria & benchmarks for a 6-week POC. Action items and timeline agreed at end. Transcript below; transcription has some minor mislabels and a few imperfect words (auto-generated).

Topics:
- PrivateLink vs VPC peering tradeoffs
- Cross-region data residency and allowed regions (US-EAST, EU-WEST, AP-SOUTHEAST)
- Egress constraints (no public egress allowed for PHI, restrict to specific NAT/EGW)
- Benchmark targets: throughput and p95 latency, example prompts and token sizes
- Success criteria, timeline (pilot + POC), and next steps

Transcript body:
00:00 Jordan: All right, hey everyone thanks for joining; can we do quick roll call, say who you are?
00:08 Liam: Yeah hi, Liam O'Connor here, Head of Platform at Medivance.
00:11 Maya: Maya Chen, security lead.
00:13 Ravi: Ravi Singh, CTO.
00:16 Olivia: Olivia Park DevOps.
00:18 Jordan: Great, Jordan Blake from Redwood, with Sana and Theo on the technical side. Quick agenda: private networking patterns, residency, egress, and what benchmarks we want to run for the POC.
00:32 Sana: Hi all, we'll focus on where you want traffic to terminate, whether you need cross-region isolation, and what the acceptable latency/cost tradeoffs are.
00:40 Liam: Our main blocker is data residency - anything touching PHI needs to stay in our tenant in us-east-1 or eu-west-1 depending on the customer. We also can't allow public internet egress from anything that handles PHI.
00:56 Maya: Correct, plus we need audit logs forwarded to our Splunk instance and key management - we use an internal HSM (Entrust) and will want KMS integration or bring-your-own-key for encryption in transit at rest.
01:12 Theo: Understood; Redwood supports PrivateLink for AWS and VPC peering in our Private deployment. PrivateLink gives you explicit interface endpoints and avoids cross-account route table changes; peering is simpler for high-throughput but needs careful CIDR planning and routing.
01:28 Ravi: What about egress charges and network throughput? Some of our models will stream lots of tokens.
01:34 Sana: Good call. For throughput-heavy workloads we recommend dedicated capacity and colocating in the same region to avoid cross-AZ egress. For PrivateLink, there's an extra cost per ENI and potential per-GB charges, but it isolates the traffic. VPC peering can be cheaper for sustained high throughput but needs non-overlapping CIDRs and we're careful about transitive routing.
01:54 Olivia: We use a transit gateway for some workloads - would that be a problem?
01:58 Theo: Transit Gateway works; we just need the TGW attachments and allowlist for the Redwood subnets. We'll provide a network checklist. A few customers use TGW + PrivateLink where peering is not feasible.
02:12 Liam: Region-wise, we want the control plane in our region and data residency guarantees for inference tokens. Can Redwood pin requests to region-specific endpoints?
02:22 Jordan: Yes, Redwood Private can be deployed in-region and you can request regional endpoints. For hosted Shared accounts we do geo-routing, but for the POC we'd recommend a dedicated Private deployment in your us-east-1 account (or a VPC/VPN peered deployment) to meet residency.
02:37 Maya: For audit and compliance we need: SOC 2/ISO artifacts, network flow logs, and proof of KMS integration. Also SLA around retention of logs.
02:46 Jordan: We'll share our SOC2 snapshot and an operations doc on log retention and KMS patterns.
02:51 Ravi: For success criteria, what are reasonable latency targets? Our UI needs p95 generation under 400ms for short prompts and under 1.2s for long chats. Throughput target 1k concurrent short requests during peak.
03:06 Sana: That seems feasible with dedicated capacity and batching tuned. For the benchmark we'll define two workloads: a short prompt workload (avg 64 tokens out, 32 in) with p95 < 400ms, and a chat workload (avg 512 tokens) with p95 < 1.2s. Throughput test: sustain 1k concurrent short requests at tail latency target.
03:28 Olivia: Do you have recommended quantization or model variants? We want to balance cost.
03:32 Theo: We'll suggest model variants and quantization profiles; for POC we can run the same model family across a couple of quantization settings to compare latency/cost. We'll include a recommended config in the benchmark plan.
03:44 Liam: Network constraints: everything handling PHI cannot leave our VPC publicly. We want encryption in motion and at rest using our KMS. Also, can we have egress constrained so that any third-party calls are blocked?
03:58 Sana: Yes - we can lock down egress to specific endpoints and only allow traffic to Redwood private endpoints. We'll need the list of service endpoints and IP ranges; for PrivateLink you'll create interface endpoints in your VPC.
04:12 Maya: What about cross-region backups or logs that might end up in a different jurisdiction? We need confirmation logs and any telemetry stay in-region.
04:20 Jordan: We can configure log sinks to forward to your Splunk in-region; telemetry can be scoped. For Private deployments all control plane metadata stays in the deployment region unless you opt into multi-region.
04:32 Ravi: Ok timeline: we're aiming to start the POC next week, run for 6 weeks, and decide on Dedicated/reserved capacity by end of Q1. Is that realistic?
04:41 Jordan: Yes - sample timeline we propose: week 0-1: network setup & security review, week 2: benchmarks and initial throughput tuning, weeks 3-5: workload soak and regression tests + integration, week 6: recap and decision.
04:55 Olivia: Any pre-work we should do?
04:57 Jordan: Provide VPC details, required CIDRs, security contacts, and compliance checklist. We'll send a PrivateLink/peering checklist and a benchmark plan.
05:05 Maya: Let's talk about the benchmark specifics now - what do you need from us?
05:08 Sana: We'll need sample prompts, typical token sizes, concurrency patterns, expected qps, and a short list of failure scenarios to test (e.g., KV cache cold start, dropping network packets).
05:20 Liam: We can provide a representative dataset of 50 prompts and a chat replay set. We have two main workloads: interactive chat (long context) and high-throughput short triggers.
05:31 Theo: Perfect. For the POC we'll run: 1) baseline latency with 10 RPS single client, 2) ramp to 1k concurrent short requests for throughput, 3) long-chat p95 under target, 4) cold KV cache test to measure warmup. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, token/sec, and cost per 1M tokens.
05:53 Ravi: Are there any gotchas with PrivateLink around DNS or ALB?
05:58 Theo: PrivateLink creates interface ENIs and you resolve via the endpoint DNS. You may need to set up private hosted zones or conditional forwarders if you use custom DNS. Also ensure your security groups allow the interface endpoints. ALB isn't required unless you want LB in front of your services.
06:14 Olivia: For Transit Gateway patterns, we need to confirm non-transitive peering restrictions - TGW -> VPC -> PrivateLink should be ok?
06:21 Sana: It works but we need the attachments documented. We'll include TGW specifics in the checklist.
06:28 Maya: Security question - does Redwood support SAML SSO for the console and RBAC for team separation?
06:33 Jordan: Yes, SAML SSO and role-based access are supported. For Private deployments you can integrate with your IdP and we'll map roles.
06:40 Liam: Any specific audit hooks so we can have immutable logs for model inferences?
06:44 Theo: We emit request traces and audit logs; for PII/PHI you can opt to redact or store logs in your S3 bucket via the log sink. We can push logs to your Splunk or S3 in-region.
06:58 Ravi: Ok, let's set preliminary success criteria now so we have measurable pass/fail: 1) p95 short prompts < 400ms, 2) p95 long chat < 1.2s, 3) sustained 1k concurrent short requests for 30m without error rate > 1%, 4) private networked connection via either PrivateLink or VPC peering with no public egress for PHI path, 5) KMS integration and SOC2 artifacts provided.
07:31 Jordan: I'll document that and include it in the POC plan. Any objections?
07:35 Maya: Sounds good. For encryption key usage we want to test a rotate-key scenario.
07:39 Theo: We'll include key rotation in the test plan and validate access logs.
07:44 Olivia: For the benchmark run, can we control traffic origin IPs to estimate egress routing costs?
07:48 Sana: Yes, control over egress nodes is possible. We'll help you isolate traffic from specific subnets to measure egress and associated charges.
07:58 Liam: Regarding timing, we prefer the network deep-dive on Friday (2027-01-15) - can Redwood's network eng join?
08:03 Jordan: Yes, we'll propose slots and bring a Redwood network engineer.
08:07 Ravi: For the POC appliance, do you need access to our staging environment or can we run entirely in your private account?
08:15 Theo: For strict residency and PHI constraints we recommend deploying Redwood Private inside your account (VPC + IAM roles). If that's not possible we can do VPC peering from our dedicated account but that increases audit work.
08:29 Maya: Deploying in our account is preferred. We'll need deployment playbooks and an installation runbook.
08:36 Jordan: We'll provide the runbook and a small terraform module for the POC.
08:40 Olivia: Anything else on compliance?
08:42 Maya: Just need to ensure logging retention policy meets our 7-year retention for audit records - does Redwood allow configurable retention?
08:48 Jordan: Yes, retention and export can be configured; we'll include retention options in the doc.
08:53 Liam: Ok let's recap next steps.
08:55 Jordan: Recap: Jordan to send PrivateLink/VPC peering checklist, SOC2 snapshot, and benchmark plan by 2027-01-13. Medivance to share VPC CIDRs, security contacts, and sample prompts by 2027-01-11. Schedule network deep-dive for 2027-01-15. POC to start week of 2027-01-18 with a 6-week run.
09:18 Ravi: Sounds good.
09:20 Maya: Thanks everyone.
09:22 Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up in email and Notion with the plan.

End of recording.
